intent: I have an acre or more on the SR 13 river corridor and I want a practice green out in the yard. Do I need anyone's permission to clear the trees and lay it, and how far back from the river does it have to stop?
distinctValue: Resolves, from St. Johns County's own Land Development Code, that the county's tree and land-clearing exemption is drawn at the one-acre line and therefore lands on Switzerland the opposite way round from its suburban neighbours. LDC Sec. 4.01.05.C.11 exempts an existing single-family home from the Land Clearing and Protected Tree Removal permit only on a Lot of Record of one (1.0) acre or less; on a Lot of Record larger than an acre the exemption reaches only the land within one hundred (100) feet of the perimeter of the house, and wherever it reaches it never covers a Specimen Tree, a conservation area or a buffer. Fruit Cove, Julington Creek Plantation and St. Johns are platted at a quarter-acre and smaller, so their whole lot falls inside the exemption; on an acre-plus parcel the part a green would actually use is commonly outside it and needs a permit drawn on a filed Site Plan, obtained through the county's clearance sheet process. Article VI Table 6.01 is carried for the acre itself: the county's own minimum Lot Area is one acre in RS-E and one acre for a Single Family Dwelling in Open Rural. The page does NOT assert which district any Switzerland parcel is in - no zoning map was opened - and tells the reader to find their district and pull their recorded acreage instead. The record also carries the county's Specimen Tree thresholds (live oak 50 inches DBH, sand live oak 49, laurel oak 48, southern magnolia 61), the two different specimen rules either side of the 100-foot ring, the hand-excavation and root-pruning requirement inside a Historic or Specimen Tree's Protected Area, the rule that a preserved tree compacted or regraded by machinery counts as Removed, and the county's upland buffer along wetland edges (generally 50 feet landward of the state wetland line on tidally influenced water, or 25 feet plus a 25-foot building setback on other contiguous wetlands, and none at all on an isolated wetland) with the Development Review Division contact to ask which applies.

sources.label: St. Johns County Land Development Code, Article IV, Sec. 4.01.05 Trees and Other Vegetation (edition of August 11, 2025)
supports: Sec. 4.01.05 Trees and Other Vegetation

A Permit will be issued after proper application and approval by St. Johns County which clearly demonstrates compliance with this Code. This Permit authorizes the Land Clearing, Grubbing, or Removal of Protected Trees and Understory vegetation only as depicted on an accompanying Site Plan.

Specimen and Historic Trees, as defined in Section 4.01.05.D shall not be impacted unless as allowed by the County Administrator or his designee upon showing of good cause, and where the Owner/Applicant proposes an alternative prepared by a Certified Arborist which conforms to the general intent and spirit of these regulations, and where the objectives of this Article have been substantially met.
B. General Prohibitions — 1. To perform Protected Tree Removal, damage any Protected Tree, or Land Clearing without a valid County Permit.

2. To perform any Construction activity, including Land Clearing and Protected Tree Removal, without first erecting Tree Protection Barricades to at least include the Protected or preserved Tree's Protected Area as defined in this Code.
3. To change earth grade within the required Protected Area of any preserved Protected Tree unless approved by the County Administrator.
4. To modify drainage which causes water to be trapped within a required Protected Area of any preserved Protected Tree.

C. Exemptions ... None of these exemptions shall apply to any Dune vegetation seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line or to a Specimen Tree, or Historic Tree, unless otherwise stated below. The burden of proving entitlement to any particular exemption shall lie with the Person claiming the exemption.

11. Land Clearing or Protected Tree Removal for existing single family residential home sites situated on a Lot of Record one (1.0) acre or less in size; except that Historic and Specimen Trees shall not be removed without obtaining approval from the County Administrator unless diseased or a substantial threat to the existing house. Furthermore, the same exemption shall apply to land within one hundred (100) feet of the perimeter of an existing single family residential home situated on a Lot of Record larger than one (1.0) acre. Newly constructed single family residential homes shall become exempt upon the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy.
8. The mowing or underbrushing of a land area that does not disturb the soil profile when conducted without disturbance, damage or Removal of Protected Trees.

3. Specimen Tree Designation — Any Native Tree of a species listed in Table 4.01.05.D.3.a Specimen Tree Thresholds with a DBH in accordance with the thresholds on the table is a Specimen Tree unless excepted by paragraph 4, below:

Table 4.01.05.D.3.a Specimen Tree Thresholds (Specimen Tree Minimum DBH, inches): Oak, Live 50; Oak, Sand Live 49; Oak, Laurel 48; Oak, Water 44; Oak, Bluff 29; Magnolia, Southern 61; Magnolia, Sweetbay 36; Cypress, Bald 125; Cypress, Pond 56; Red Cedar, Eastern 43; Red Maple 47; American Elm 43; Hickory, Pignut 43; Sweetgum 37; Sycamore 53; River Birch 23.

5. On sites where grade cuts are necessary under Historic or Specimen Trees proper root pruning shall be required. Within the Tree's Protected Area, all excavation shall be by hand, and roots two (2) inches and larger shall be evenly cut.

7. A Tree Protection Barricade shall be installed at the Protected Area of each Specimen Tree and shall be inspected by the County prior to the initiation of any Construction activity on site and shall remain in place throughout Construction.

G. Determination of Protected Area — The Protected Area shall be the Drip Line of a Protected Tree. A Tree Protection Barricade shall be installed at the Drip Line, unless an alternative is approved by the County Administrator. No Land Clearing or Tree Removal shall begin until after the Protection Barricades are installed and the Barricades shall remain in place until after completion of Construction.

Any preserved Tree damaged during Construction will be considered Removed and will have to be replaced. Damage may include, but is not limited to, mechanical damage resulting in the removal of bark, limbs, leaders, and sign attachment, or root damage resulting from grade changes, Utility installation, excessive scraping, removal of Understory, and compaction from heavy machinery.

c. Development of Individual Residential Lots — (1) No Land Clearing or Protected Tree Removal shall be allowed before receiving an approved Site Plan. Applications for such approval shall be submitted complete with a scaled detailed Site Plan showing all Lot characteristics and dimensions, all existing and proposed Construction Improvements, all fill including septic mounds, onsite sanitary disposal tanks and any wells.

(2) For purposes of this Code, all Protected Trees in any area with six (6) inches or more grade change shall be considered Removed and no Tree inches shall be given for such Trees. At Final Inspection County personnel shall verify forty (40) Tree inches per acre exist, either preserved or planted in the Lot area.

3. Permits required by this Code may be obtained after-the-fact for Land Clearing and/or Tree Removal activities upon determination by the County Administrator that such activities were performed in accordance with Permit issuance criteria specified in this Section.
Page footer establishing the edition read: "St. Johns County Land Development Code IV-7 August 11, 2025".

SCOPE NOTE for the specimen-tree carve-out: the phrase "diseased or a substantial threat to the existing house" appears once in Article IV, inside exemption C.11, and C.11 is scoped to a Lot of Record one (1.0) acre or less and, on a larger Lot of Record, to the land within one hundred (100) feet of the perimeter of the home. Outside that reach the governing sentence is Sec. 4.01.05.A: "Specimen and Historic Trees, as defined in Section 4.01.05.D shall not be impacted unless as allowed by the County Administrator or his designee upon showing of good cause, and where the Owner/Applicant proposes an alternative prepared by a Certified Arborist which conforms to the general intent and spirit of these regulations, and where the objectives of this Article have been substantially met." The page states both rules and which side of the ring each governs; it no longer says "on a lot of any size".

SCOPE NOTE for hand excavation: Sec. 4.01.05.D.5 is written for Historic or Specimen Trees only, not for every Protected Tree - "On sites where grade cuts are necessary under Historic or Specimen Trees proper root pruning shall be required. Within the Tree's Protected Area, all excavation shall be by hand, and roots two (2) inches and larger shall be evenly cut." Sec. G supplies the geometry for any Protected Tree - "The Protected Area shall be the Drip Line of a Protected Tree" - so a Specimen Tree's Protected Area is its Drip Line. The page now says "under a specimen or historic tree ... inside its drip line".
Page footers sampled IV-1 through IV-10 read "St. Johns County Land Development Code IV-n August 11, 2025".

sources.label: St. Johns County: Development Review — Land Clearing / Landscaping, Wetlands and Upland Buffers
supports: The Environmental Development Review Section reviews all proposed development applications including Comprehensive Plan Amendments, Rezonings, Commercial Projects and Single Family Residential for compliance with the environmental components of the County's Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code. The key issues include upland buffers for wetlands, listed species protection, County protected habitats and species, tree protection, and landscaping.
County Natural Resource Regulations are in Article IV of the Land Development Code.
Single Family Residential requirements are found in section 4.01.05 and are outlined in Section 17 of the Development Review Manual.

Do I need a permit to clear land in St. Johns County? Any type of land disturbance activities involving vegetation removal, root raking or under brushing may need a permit from the county prior to starting. The issues involved in the review of the activity include proposed changes in drainage patterns, identification and protection of protected species, erosion and sedimentation control measures.

Lot clearing for residential home sites is permitted through the clearance sheet process. Clearance sheet application information can be found in section 17 of the St. Johns County Development Review Manual.
A tally of 40 tree inches per acre must be preserved or planted on a lot. For example, if a lot is .25 acres, 10 inches of trees must be preserved or planted on the lot.

Tree removal on lots less than one acre with an existing home do not require a tree removal permit, as long as the tree is not a specimen tree and the tree does not lie within a conservation area or buffer.
Residential lots that fall under the Ponte Vedra Zoning area (Ordinance 20-38) require a tree removal permit to remove any protected trees.
What is an upland buffer and when is it required? An upland buffer is a strip of land along the edge of wetland areas to remain undisturbed with all existing vegetation.

Generally, a 50-foot upland buffer is required landward of the state jurisdictional wetland line for all tidally-influenced water bodies up to the point where a Mean High Water Line can be set and a 25-foot upland buffer with an additional 25-foot building setback from the buffer is required from all other contiguous wetland areas. Isolated wetland areas, or closed depressions surrounded by uplands, do not require a County upland buffer.
Different sized upland buffers are required depending on the type of development project, type of wetland, or location.
Wetland areas are protected by law and must remain in their natural condition.
The department contact number published in the page footer of this Development Review section is (904) 209-0675.

NEGATIVE FINDING: this page's Land Clearing / Landscaping section answers five questions about permits, tree cover and irrigation and never mentions artificial or synthetic turf; the county's irrigation rule on it applies to "Commercial and New Residential Common Areas only".

CONFLICT NOTE on the acre: this page reads "Tree removal on lots less than one acre with an existing home do not require a tree removal permit", while LDC Sec. 4.01.05.C.11 reads "one (1.0) acre or less in size". A Lot of Record of exactly 1.00 acre is exempt under the Code and not exempt under this web page. The page copy follows the Code, which is the controlling instrument, and no longer cites this web page as reinforcing the acre line. This page is cited only for the two conditions on the exemption (not a specimen tree, not within a conservation area or buffer), for land disturbance, and for the clearance sheet and upland buffers.

BUFFER SCOPE: the same answer states "Different sized upland buffers are required depending on the type of development project, type of wetland, or location" and "Isolated wetland areas, or closed depressions surrounded by uplands, do not require a County upland buffer." An upland buffer exists only where there is a wetland edge, so the 50-foot and 25-foot figures are not an exhaustive pair of outcomes. The page now carries the variability, the isolated-wetland exception and the instruction to ask the county whether the parcel carries a mapped wetland line.

The phone number (904) 209-0675 appears on this page only in the sidebar as "Dept. Contact". It is not published here as a number for the Environmental Development Review Section. The page copy now attributes it to the Development Review Division, per the contacts page below.

sources.label: St. Johns County: Tree Information for Residential Home Sites (Development Review Manual Section 17.0.5 worksheet, revised May 2026)
supports: St. Johns County Tree Information for Residential Home Sites
If the lot is within a subdivision, PUD, or PRD with an approved NSP, please refer to the NSP for minimum tree requirements.

If existing trees are to be used to meet the minimum tree requirement, provide the locations, types, and diameters of those trees on the site plan. The diameter of an existing tree is measured at 4.5 feet above the ground.
Any trees that meet specimen criteria as defined in section 4.01.05.D of the Land Development Code must be shown on the site plan.

Trees may not be planted or preserved for tree inch value if they are located within easements or wetlands. The areas of all easements and wetlands may be subtracted from the lot size area when calculating the minimum tree inch requirement.

Canopy trees - Trees that will attain a mature canopy of 30 feet wide by 35 feet tall. Examples include laurel and live oak, pecan, hickory, elm, river birch, maple, sycamore, red cedar, magnolia, poplar, cypress, and pines.
Document footer: "Revised May 2026".

supports: Sec. 6.01.01 Schedule Of District Area, Height, Bulk, and Placement Regulations - Except as specifically provided elsewhere in this Code, regulations governing the Minimum Lot Width, Minimum Lot Area, Maximum Lot Coverage, Floor Area Ratio, Impervious Surface Ratio, Minimum Yard Requirements, and Maximum Height of Structures shall be established for the districts as shown in the following Table 6.01:

TABLE 6.01 SCHEDULE OF AREA, HEIGHT, BULK AND PLACEMENT STANDARDS - row "RS-E": Minimum Lot Widths "150 feet"; Minimum Lot Area "1 acre"; Maximum Lot Coverage by All Buildings "20%"; Impervious Surface Ratio "70%"; Min. Yard Req. "30/20/20 feet"; Maximum Height of Structures "35 feet".

TABLE 6.01 - row "OR - Single Family Dwelling or Mobile Home": Minimum Lot Widths "100 feet"; Minimum Lot Area "1 acre"; Maximum Lot Coverage by All Buildings "35%"; Impervious Surface Ratio "70%". Row "OR - All Other Uses": "100 feet"; "1 acre"; "20%".
TABLE 6.01 footnote on the RS-E and OR Minimum Lot Area cells: "See Section 6.01.05 for Minimum Lot Area and Lot Width with use of septic tank and/or private well."
TABLE 6.01 footnote: "Yard requirements may be modified by additional setback requirements for Lots adjacent to contiguous Wetlands contained in Section 4.01.06 of this Code."

Sec. 6.01.05 Minimum Lot Area By Available Utilities - TABLE 6.02 Minimum Lot Area and Width Based on Utilities: "Private Well and Private Septic Tank - 43,560 square feet - 100 feet"; "Central Water and Private Septic Tanks - 21,780 square feet - 100 feet"; "Private Well and Central Wastewater - 10,890 square feet - 75 feet". Preamble: "In addition to the Minimum Zoning Lot Area requirements specified in 6.01.01, the following regulations shall apply to all new residential Subdivisions (platted or legal and documented Lots of Record existing prior to the initial effective date of this Code are exempt from these requirements). Where there is a conflict with Section 6.01.01, the greater standard shall apply."

NEGATIVE FINDING: the word "turf" does not appear anywhere in Article VI. The only artificial-vegetation provision is Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 - "Non-living ground cover, such as rocks, gravel, and mulch, may be used in combination with living plant material. The use of artificial plants shall not be permitted to meet any of the landscaping requirements." Part 6.06.00 attaches to Development Permits for constructing a Building or off-street Parking Area (Sec. 6.06.01.A), not to a homeowner replacing a lawn.
